assumptions: Existing accepted tasks and prepared source-free images are reused.
One meaningful scoped environment per suitable PR, with deterministic verification, wrong and valid controls, one blind Sonnet rollout and reviewed trace.
At most three consolidated repair rounds per run, with an explicit unresolved outcome at the limit.
Small real models, local data and pinned offline assets; actual CUDA or distributed execution for hardware-dependent claims.
Inference and cloud compute only; no engineer labor, training on the resulting tasks or repeated solver evaluation sweeps.
limitations: Per-repository ranges are planning estimates based on list composition and observed campaigns; they are not measured marginal costs for every remaining PR.
Native hardware validation for AMD ROCm, AWS Neuron and some specialized kernels needs additional provider support and hardware scoping.
Maintenance-only changes may not support a useful coding task without broadening beyond the PR.
Unknown historical reservations are not counted as confirmed charges or automatically reclaimed.
Tokenizers requires Rust source collection and verifier support; current Tasksmith export accepts Python source changes. Budget excludes human engineering labor.
Observed acceptance includes engineering intervention. Estimate assumes continued assistance and excludes assistant-session usage outside the campaign ledger; unattended full-list yield is unproven.

observed_cost_anchors.scope: Recorded model usage and conservative compute estimates, including failed or unfinished attempts; not provider invoices.
